title: Television Channels
summary: Television keeps all types of audiences in mind (children, women, youth, elderly, farmers, workers, students, illiterates) and offers special audience programmes: children's (stories, music, games, general knowledge), women's (cooking, sewing, legal tips), farmers' (agriculture, dairy, poultry, cooperatives), youth (discussion of problems by young anchors) and educational or school telecasts. Categories of channels: news channels (round-the-clock; Hindi: Aaj Tak, Star News, Zee News, NDTV India; English: NDTV 24x7, CNBC-TV18, Times Now, Headlines Today; also regional languages); sports channels (live sports events, sports news; the first sports channel was ESPN, which began in 1979 in the US); cartoon channels (the most popular with children, e.g. Pogo and Cartoon Network showing Tom and Jerry, Scooby-Doo, Popeye and Indian cartoons like Akbar and Birbal, Tenali Raman); entertainment and lifestyle channels (home, garden, kitchen, family; Zoom, Discovery Travel and Living); science and discovery channels (weather, technology, space, nature; National Geographic and Discovery).

The basic objective of television is to inform, entertain and educate; 'infotainment' and 'edutainment' are new words. Informative programmes: news and current affairs (bulletins, commentaries, interviews, panel discussions), sports programmes (cricket matches, sports diaries), cookery and food shows (Khana Khazana), and programmes on environment, science and technology and economic policies (Surabhi, Bharat Ek Khoj). Entertainment programmes: serials, soap operas and plays (Ghar Ek Mandir), comedy shows, musical programmes (Ghazal Goshthi), game shows, chat shows (Koffee with Karan), cartoons, fairy tales, horror shows (Aahat) and reality shows (Indian Idol, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa). Educational programmes: open university and distance learning (UGC, IGNOU), social and development programmes (health, hygiene, agriculture, literacy, family planning) and culture and gender studies programmes; Gyandarshan is the educational channel of Doordarshan.

Two broad formats: fiction (based on imagination and dramatization, meant for entertainment: serials and soap operas such as Hum Log, Ghar Ek Mandir; the name 'soap opera' comes from radio serials sponsored by soap manufacturers; serials rely on a continuing plot, episode by episode; film-based programmes mix formats) and non-fiction (based on real incidents and events): news bulletins (summary of stories in order of importance; 24-hour channels have replaced the half-hour bulletin), game or quiz shows (Bournvita Quiz Contest presented by Derek O'Brien) and talks and discussion programmes (a regular host interviews guests, audience participation by phone, segments separated by advertisements: We the People, Muqabla).

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) Reality shows are a type of ______ programme. (ii) Television programmes are broadly classified into ______ categories.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are nature and science related channels.
Match: (i) Cartoon Network (ii) ESPN (iii) Discovery (iv) NDTV 24x7 with (a) science (b) sports (c) children (d) news.
State true or false: (i) Comedy shows are entertainment programmes. (ii) Culture and gender studies programmes are informative.
Name two special audience programmes on television.
Children's programmes and women's programmes (also youth and farmers').
vsa: Name any two categories of television channels with an example of each.
News channels – Aaj Tak; sports channels – ESPN (also cartoon – Pogo).
New words for programmes that combine information or education with entertainment, in which entertainment is common.
A continuing episodic dramatic serial; the name comes from radio serials sponsored by soap makers.
Give two examples of educational programmes.
Open university and distance learning (UGC, IGNOU) programmes and health, agriculture or literacy campaigns; Gyandarshan.
sa: Discuss three types of informative television programmes with examples.

News and current affairs (bulletins, panel discussions); sports programmes (cricket matches, sports diaries); cookery and food shows (Khana Khazana); also science and environment programmes (Surabhi).
Describe the categories of television channels.
News, sports, cartoon, entertainment and lifestyle, and science and discovery channels, each for a different audience.
Explain the types of entertainment programmes with examples.
Serials and soaps, comedy shows, musical programmes, game and chat shows, cartoons, fairy tales, horror and reality shows like Indian Idol.
la: Differentiate between fiction and non-fiction television programme formats with examples in each category.

Fiction is imaginative and dramatized for entertainment (serials such as Ghar Ek Mandir, soap operas, film-based programmes); non-fiction is based on real events and information (news bulletins, quiz shows like Bournvita Quiz Contest, talks and discussions like We the People).
Discuss the various categories of television channels in detail, giving examples.
News (Aaj Tak, NDTV 24x7), sports (ESPN), cartoon (Pogo, Cartoon Network), entertainment and lifestyle (Zoom) and science and discovery (National Geographic, Discovery) channels.
